summary: All 300+ examples pass and there are no errors or blocking open questions. The only open question, OQ-calculator-coverage, is non-blocking. Nothing from the previous review is fully resolved. The biggest gap is the 'incomplete - HR must complete' state after an HR change. Its scope is still undefined, and three major dev-refinement questions remain. The tariff_code trace warning still shows the old child-digit expression. Engineering can start on the main flow, but PO decisions are needed on the incomplete state, the tariff_code expression and the tech leaks.

findings.title: Scope of the 'incomplete - HR must complete' state is undefined
findings.why: D-052 and D-053 cover the tariff letter and church-tax suffix only. The following are not covered: pension fund canton, fund civil status Married without a spouse date of birth, an undeterminable child digit, and an undeterminable 'subject to source tax' after an HR change. Engineering would have to guess.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement US-01.6 (major); feature.md x2 (major); D-052, D-053
findings.action: Add a decision listing every derived result that can show 'incomplete'. Cover canton, spouse date of birth, child digit and subject-to-source-tax, and state what each shows when its inputs were never asked.

findings.title: AC-06.6.5 examples: expectations after an HR change are ambiguous
findings.why: The examples now pass, but the first still expects Denomination 'required', which contradicts D-053. The second omits the never-asked spouse-employment answer. The test may assert the wrong thing.
findings.action: Rewrite both examples to expect 'HR must complete' for the unasked answers. Show the spouse-employment input in the second example.

findings.title: tariff_code expression vs child-digit statement
findings.why: The trace judge still reports if_else(child_count,1,0), which only gives 0 or 1. D-052 requires the number of counted children (for example C3Y). Codes for two or more children would be wrong. The report may predate the D-052 override.
findings.action: Confirm the expression after D-052 yields the child count, and add an example with 2 or more children.

findings.title: Technical wording leaks into the spec
findings.why: D-045 forbids internal-formula language. 'ISO 3166' is implementation vocabulary, and 'free text is not accepted' dictates how the input behaves.
findings.evidence: tech_leak: feature.md and information.md ('internal expression'); US-02.3; item.address_country, nationality, spouse_nationality; AC-02.3.1, AC-05.1.2, AC-05.2.3
findings.action: Replace these with business wording: 'chosen from a list of countries, plus stateless'. Drop the 'internal expression' sentence and the free-text sentence.

findings.title: Rules rely on facts and gating that no cited source backs
findings.why: The following are unbacked or cited incorrectly: Liechtenstein/non_return_days_45 gating, tariff purposes, 'G→Q cannot occur', and rows citing facts missing from the rule's citation list. This weakens traceability.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: questionnaire_flow, base_tariff_letter, cross_border_tariff, tariff_letter, calculator_residence, pension_fund_canton, liechtenstein_no_source_tax, has_children, child_*, spouse_gainful_employment; D-002, D-047 not cited
findings.action: Add the missing citations (D-002, D-047, the cited calculator facts). Mark the remaining rows as inferred decisions.

findings.title: G→Q mapping kept although D-006 drops G/Q
findings.why: Row 6 of the tariff letter rule (D-051) conflicts with D-006 and with the base letter rule. This risks dead code and unneeded tests.
findings.action: Decide whether to remove the G→Q row or keep it with a stated reason.

findings.title: Unconfirmed rule: at least one child block required
findings.why: AC-07.2.1 requires at least one child block and every child question to be required. No source backs either. What happens when the last block is removed is undefined.
findings.action: Confirm the rule with HR. Define what happens when the last block is removed (blocked, or 'has children' becomes no).

findings.title: Inconsistent expected values across example tables
findings.why: 'asked' and 'required' are used for the same question. '–' is used as both input and result with mismatched values. Spouse date of birth expectations differ between Married/Single and Divorced/Widowed.
findings.action: Define the vocabulary: asked vs required, and what '–' means. Normalise the tables.

findings.title: Conflicting rules on when a missing answer blocks the employee
findings.why: Some stories block leaving the step and others block only submission. US-01.7 allows saving a partly filled step.
findings.action: Decide: block submission only (recommended), and align the stories.

findings.title: Calculator coverage unverified; minor semantics open
findings.why: The unexplored tariff paths (A/B/H residence block, inferred per-child rows, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N) could give wrong codes. Several calculator facts are only partly verified. Also open: certificate 'provided' vs 'has', the 'sent' date for the start-date check, and the insurance start-date error behaviour (F-pension_portal-e45e5b unused).
findings.evidence: OQ-calculator-coverage (non-blocking); fact_judge F-zh_source_tax_calculator-037b1c, 64ac33, dc0ae9, c8aa5e, 2754e8; dev_refinement US-08.2, US-03.1; coverage
findings.action: Have a domain expert compare computed codes with the calculator before go-live. Clarify certificate wording, the 'sent' date, and the start-date error behaviour.
